role: Registry Responsibility Review — Agent AA vs. 600-Series
purpose: Clarify the relationship between 'Agent AA' (referenced in the program spec) and the deferred 600-Series. Ensure Agent AA activities do not constitute 600-Series activation. Establish the governance boundary.
research_methodology: Cross-referenced S600 Charter §4 Agent Definitions, S725 Portfolio Stewardship Framework Lane 600, S601 Agent C Registry Operations Review, and AGENTS.md §5 Dual Verification. Searched for 'Agent AA' references across all repository documentation.

agent_aa_identity.search_results: No reference to 'Agent AA' found in S600 Charter, S725 Stewardship Framework, S601 outputs, S724 Operating Model, REVISION_HISTORY.md, or any governance document.
agent_aa_identity.interpretation: Agent AA appears to be a reference from the S602 program specification, not a previously defined agent in the governance framework. It is best interpreted as the registry-script maintainer or registry-operations role referenced in the S600 Charter §4.1 (Agent A: Registry Operations) and S601 Agent C findings.

closest_governance_mappings.role: Existing registry scripts (build_master_registry.js, generate_registry.js) and artifacts (registry/ directory) — no dedicated maintainer
QID inventory cross-check against MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md — verification, not maintenance

agent_aa_identity.assumption: Agent AA = registry-operations function (not a specific agent ID). Covers: (a) build-script maintenance, (b) registry artifact verification, (c) QID inventory management. Currently distributed across 700-series (verification) and build scripts (generation) with no single agent owner.

agent_aa_is_not_600_activation.verdict: TRUE — Agent AA registry operations do NOT constitute 600-series activation.

evidence.definitional: 600-series activation per S600 Charter §5 requires ALL 4 mandatory gates (Economic, Board, Ownership, Baseline) to PASS. Registry operations — whether performed by a 700-series Governance Auditor, a build script, or any agent — are operational maintenance activities, not lane activation.
evidence.scope: S600 Charter §2.1 authorizes registry operations as ONE of six 600-series domains. Registry maintenance alone is insufficient to constitute 600-series activation — the lane would also need EW template libraries (§4.2), draft preparation support (§4.3), and standards library maintenance (§4.4) simultaneously activated. A single domain operation does not activate the lane.
evidence.precedent: Registry artifacts (registry/ directory) were created during S314/S315 under 700/800-series authority — not 600-series. Build scripts (build_master_registry.js, generate_registry.js) were created under 700-series governance — not 600-series. These are operational utilities, not lane-activation events.
evidence.governance: Any activation requires a new Executive Board vote per S600 §5.2 and S725 Lane 600 Succession Plan. An agent performing registry maintenance does not hold an Executive Board vote. No vote = no activation.

operations.authority: 700-series Governance Auditor (S725 Row 17 — verification includes build-script integrity)
operations.not_600_activation_because: Build scripts are operational tooling, not 600-series domain artifacts

operations.authority: 700-series T0 protocol (S725 Lane 700 — cross-check QID inventory as standard audit)
operations.not_600_activation_because: Verification is governance, not content operations

operations.authority: Must be authorized by Governance Auditor as a 700-series operational artifact, not a 600-series domain artifact
operations.not_600_activation_because: A similarity ledger is an operational tool consumed by certification (800) and governance (700) — its creation does not require the full 600-series charter activation
operations.risk: If created under 700-series authority, must not be attributed to 600-series in documentation or metadata

operations.authority: 700-series (S725 Row 17) — registry integrity monitoring is a governance function
operations.not_600_activation_because: Registry maintenance has been performed under 700/800 authority throughout the project lifecycle

triggers: Creating all 4 agent-domain artifacts simultaneously (not just registry)
Changing question_state on any item by 600-authority
Producing draft packets consumed by 800-series certification waves
A documented Executive Board vote authorizing 600-series activation

governance_guard_implications.if_agent_aa_writes_to_registry: MASTER_QUESTION_REGISTRY.md is governed by Rule 3 BLOCK (never hand-edit). Build scripts (generate_registry.js) are the ONLY authorized producers. Any manual edit is mechanically blocked. This serves as an additional safeguard against 600-series activation via registry overreach.

recommendation: Agent AA registry operations are 700-series governance functions, not 600-series activation. The boundary is defined by: (a) authority source (700-series authorization vs. 600-series charter), (b) scope of work (operational maintenance vs. multi-domain lane activation), and (c) governance attribution (REVISION_HISTORY.md entry specifics the lane). No further boundary clarification is required for the DEFERRED state. If and when a similarity ledger or registry index is created, the creating session must explicitly attribute the work to 700-series, not 600-series.
